newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris, Bonn agree on transport plane - report.
newsitem.headline: Paris, Bonn agree on transport plane - report.

text.p: A French defence newsletter said on Wednesday that France and Germany had reached agreement on terms for producing a future large military transport aircraft (FLA).

The weekly TTU said Defence Ministers Charles Millon and Volker Ruehe had sent their national armaments directors a confidential agreement under which Germany would commit itself to ordering a maximum 75 aircraft and France 50.
The defence ministry was not immediately able to comment.

The FLA, due to replace ageing Transall and Hercules C-130 transport planes early next century, would be produced "along commercial lines with a single development-production phase," TTU quoted the document as saying.
France stated that the planes would be paid for "in the series production phase, with the unit price including fixed and allied financial costs."
Germany said in the same document it was continuing to look for alternative methods of financing along the lines proposed by France.

Both countries said last June that because of defence budget constraints, they were unable to finance the development phase of the FLA but would buy it if European aerospace companies produced it on commercial lines.
They have also been discussing the project with Italy, Spain and Britain.
